findings: May 6, 2026 and November 7, 2026 both describe Pix as Brazil's bank-to-bank real-time method: Brazilian buyer, BRL presentment, account-country settlement currency, customer review and approval in the banking app using a QR code or Pix string. The November overview distinguishes immediate confirmation timing and settlement up to T+2 from authorization duration, which depends on the buyer. Checkout remains open, the bank app does not redirect back, and Checkout/Elements handles the configured return_url at a terminal intent state. Check that state for actual success (old raw lines 4–33, 55–106, 107–120, 168–180; new raw lines 5–21, 53–75, 228–250).

Pix Automático applies to eligible businesses outside Brazil. The customer authorizes amount and billing cycle in their banking app. SetupIntent establishes a mandate without collecting an initial payment; PaymentIntent makes an initial charge and establishes a mandate. For subsequent payments the bank pre-debit notice precedes charging by three days, the Intent is processing in this interval, and confirmation can take up to seven days with retries. Over-limit recurring payments fail. When a Charge exists its payment_method_details.pix.mandate identifies the Mandate. Merchant detachment revokes it and prevents reuse; bank-app customer revocation sends mandate.updated, then a new on-session mandate is needed (old raw lines 8–10, 94–105 and 182–186; new raw lines 79–83, 146–164 and 185–200).

The November overview makes refund, dispute and capabilities boundaries explicit. Full and partial refunds within 90 days return to the original bank account and cannot be canceled. Usually a few minutes has no guaranteed maximum; Refund object status, request acceptance and actual customer bank credit are distinct. Under MED the customer supplies evidence to their bank, Stripe notifies the merchant via email/Dashboard/charge.dispute.created, and the partner decision cannot be contested or appealed through Stripe. Debit to the Stripe account follows notified partner acceptance. Full disputes are supported; partial disputes and manual/partial/multi/over-capture are marked unsupported (old raw lines 42–52 and 140–146; new raw lines 91–144).

The November eligibility/capability and product matrices include provisional merchant/platform/marketplace access, B2B/B2C, 12 displayed prohibited MCCs, expanded support labels and explicit unsupported entries such as Terminal or Express Checkout Element. For front-end products enable in settings; manually listed integration goes through acceptance guidance. The new Connect ending reiterates the connected-account supported-country/activation condition for direct charges or on_behalf_of and distinguishes who activates by Dashboard type. Retain May platform-as-MoR route as May evidence (old raw lines 94–105, 123–138 and 148–166, 234–243; new raw lines 14–51, 85–115, 166–200 and 276–282).

The current source line 19 attributes IOF collection/remittance to Ebanx alone. Both dated guides say Stripe and its partner handle collection and remittance; separately they identify Ebanx as the default receipt sender and displayed payment recipient. Keep these operational roles separate from which party bears the dated 3.5% cross-border FX fee (customer by default, merchant absorption by choice) and who provides checkout disclosures (Stripe for Checkout/Elements, the merchant for Direct API) (source lines 19 and 29–37; old raw lines 188–203 and 214–232; new raw lines 202–217 and 252–274). contributions.original_prompts:
New raw `raw/stripe-payments-pix-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw `raw/stripe-pix-2025.md`. Current summaries `wiki/sources/source-stripe-pix.md`.

- Q1. For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/pix`, what documented behavior, prerequisites, actors and state transitions does the complete new capture establish? How do these compare with the matched prior capture and each mapped summary?

- Q2. Which changes are substantive, presentational or navigation-only? Identify the exact dated qualifications, conflicts and reciprocal routes that the proposed disposition should preserve.

reviewed_answers.Q1: https://docs.stripe.com/payments/pix describes a Brazilian buyer paying in BRL by authorizing a QR code or Pix string in their banking app. Stripe uses the account-country settlement currency, and the November guide labels confirmation immediate and settlement up to two business days. Checkout stays open during bank authorization, and a configured return at a terminal intent state requires a separate success check. For eligible Pix Automático outside Brazil, the buyer approves the amount and cycle in-app via a SetupIntent without an initial charge or a PaymentIntent with an initial payment. Later charges wait three days after pre-debit notice, remain processing and can take up to seven days with retries. A revoked mandate requires new on-session authorization. Refunds can be requested for 90 days and return to the original account, with credit distinct from request status. The bank takes evidence for limited disputes and the merchant cannot contest in Stripe. Connect direct or on_behalf_of charges require connected-account eligibility and activation. Stripe and its partner collect and remit the IOF documented at 3.5% on applicable cross-border FX. The buyer funds it by default or the merchant absorbs it. Stripe handles disclosures for Checkout/Elements, and Direct API merchants display theirs. Ebanx sends receipts by default and appears as payment recipient (old raw lines 188–203 and 214–232; new raw lines 202–217 and 252–274). See also new raw lines 9–21, 53–83, 107–200, 228–250 and 276–282, and old raw lines 8–33, 94–120 and 140–186. source-stripe-pix.md preserves the May identity but needs the newer eligibility, status, limit and refund/dispute qualifications.
reviewed_answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/pix the November reorganization and numbered checkout steps are presentational. The added bank-app and terminal-intent redirect conditions are substantive, along with provisional access, T+2 settlement wording, an account-enabled override of the default BRL equivalent of USD 3,000 per payment, and the USD 3,000/day and USD 10,000/month limits for Brazilian buyers paying a business outside Brazil (old raw lines 30–33, 94–105 and 182–186; new raw lines 12–21, 57–83). Keep that earlier Brazilian invite-only wording dated, the Brazilian one-time-only scope, the narrower Singapore non-profit restriction, unchanged conditional IOF choices, and May platform-as-MoR guidance alongside November direct/on_behalf_of activation. Preserve the new refund, dispute and mandate conditions and the separate Pix Automático and subscriptions routes, with reciprocal stripe-pix and stripe-real-time-payments routes in source-stripe-pix.md. The broader real-time matrix's SetupIntents/setup_future_usage No labels differ from the November method matrix and mandate route (new raw lines 146–200). A refund request, a terminal intent or a partner notice alone must retain its own outcome scope. The line 19 attribution to Ebanx alone is a baseline error. Both snapshots name Stripe and its partner for IOF collection/remittance, with Ebanx separately named for receipts and recipient display. Preserve who funds the dated fee and who provides disclosures as separate roles (old raw lines 188–203 and 214–232; new raw lines 202–217 and 252–274).
